title: Understanding the Matrix $X$
text: The matrix $X$ is a four-column matrix where each column represents a different variable: number of blocks, total distance, fare, and a column of all ones. This matrix is centered before applying PCA.

title: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
text: The singular value decomposition of a matrix $X$ is given by $X=U*Sigma*V**T$. Here, $U$ and $V$ are orthogonal matrices, and $Sigma$ is a diagonal matrix containing the singular values.

title: Dot Product of Columns
text: The dot product of two columns in a matrix is the sum of the products of their corresponding entries. If the dot product of the first and second columns of $V$ is equal to $$1$$, it implies a specific relationship between these columns.

title: Conclusion on the Dot Product
text: Given that $V$ is orthogonal, the dot product of any two different columns of $V$ should be $$0$$, not $$1$$. Therefore, the statement is false.
